newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela CVG remains confident on Cristinas gold.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela CVG remains confident on Cristinas gold.

text.p: The President of Venezuelan industrial giant Corporacion Venezolana de Guayana (CVG) Elias Ynaty said Thursday he was confident the Supreme Court would rule in its favor against a rival claim for the gold-rich Las Cristinas concession.
"There is no possibility that Crystallex will win," Ynaty told reporters, firing the latest salvo in what has become a raging legal battle over South America's largest gold mine.

The CVG is joint partner with Placer Dome Inc in a $576 million project to develop the concession which Crystallex say it owns after it bought local company Inversores Mael last year. Crystallex has a case pending with the Supreme Court following earlier favorable Supreme Court rulings.

"The CVG is absolutely the owner of the concessions," Ynaty said, brushing off Crystallex's arguments. "Everything is ready ... it's very likely construction will begin by the second half of July," he added.
Ynaty confirmed the CVG would be suing Crystallex, in early July, for costs related to the delay of the project.
"We have documentation that shows Mael renounced their rights to the property in return for other concessions," Ynaty said.
Crystallex lawyers argue the documents do not prejudice their claim. No date has yet been set for the Supreme Court ruling.
